review.official:
Gordon Tannen, born in
Columbia
, was promoted to Chief Inspector of the Columbian Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco,
Arts
Units, and
Originium
following the
Propeller Paradise Incident
. He has also been restored to his position as Chief Executive of
Propeller Paradise
. He has entered into cooperation with
Rhodes Island
to secure legitimate channels for our
Oripathy
medicine to enter the Columbian market, while also representing Propeller Paradise in our joint aerospace research.

files.description:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be non-infected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Skybox shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.13u/L
Operator Skybox regularly comes into contact with Originium products, resulting in heightened risk of infection.

Hope that suit of his doesn't start leaking Originium. He doesn't take it off even when he sleeps...
—Space Fin 054

[Excerpt from the Propeller Paradise Administration Rules for Secretaries]
......
04. Anticipate the boss's needs and serve tea at the right time by listening to the boss's voice and observing the scales around his mouth.
22. Respect your boss!! Stop bringing tea whenever you think he's thirsty. You're his secretary, not his mom! Stop treating him like a kid!
......
09. Do not interrupt the boss, argue with the boss, or steal the boss's words in front of other people. Actually, just shut your mouth, there's no need for you to talk.
15. Immediately remind the boss if he makes a mistake during a negotiation. If you don't, it's your fault if anything goes wrong.
......
12. Know your boss, and communicate his intentions with absolute faithfulness when negotiating, for you are his personal representative.
17. Use your brain when negotiating, don't just communicate his intentions. No one will take you seriously if they can tell you're just repeating what your boss said.
......

'Did you really spend six months under Mr. Tannen as his secretary, Mercia? Is it really possible to follow all these rules at the same time?'
'Yes. It just takes more effort. But there is also a way to make him forget all these rules and work with you in a different way.'
'Really?'
'Pay close attention to his outfit, his little robot, and all the Originium equipment and Arts units he fiddles with. Express as much interest as you can feign.'
'...And then?'
'And then, you just deal with him like you would deal with the most talkative boy in class when you were in elementary school.'
—Conversation between Mercia, former secretary to the Chief Executive of Propeller Paradise, and her successor

[Interview from the documentary Bluebeard and the Great Toothpaste Prohibition] When we talked about 'toothpaste tubes', we were talking about vehicle coolant pipes. When the Great Toothpaste Prohibition was first enacted, we filled the tubes with toothpaste and smuggled it from Kazimierz into Columbia. No one would find out unless you took the vehicle apart. You could only fool the ATAO for so long, though. Within six months, every checkpoint on the Columbian border had trained casters posted, and all it took was a wave of their wand to expose the goods. It was around that time that the name 'Bluebeard' started making its rounds. He was a mysterious figure who never showed his face, but it didn't matter. No one ever saw Mr. Max during the Revolutionary War, either. What mattered was that Bluebeard could help us avoid the checks. From anti-Arts coating to invisible tubes... he always had a way. Everybody knew the toothpaste hero who defied the authorities. They were singing songs about him: 'You can have my smokes and you can have my booze, but you can't have Bluebeard's toothpaste tube.' And you'd hear people boasting about brushing teeth with Bluebeard every night. What happened next? Heh, he sold us out and went into the ATAO. Some said he got bought out, other said he was coerced, but all we know is that we never heard from our toothpaste hero Bluebeard again. —A truck driver who worked as a smuggler during the Great Toothpaste Prohibition Gordon unabashedly describes his job at the ATAO as 'racing natives, refugees, and smugglers at the border checkpoints.' Border checkpoints are high-speed mobile platforms owned by the ATAO. They are little more than the size of a truck, but their speed is real, and smugglers call them 'toilets running with sirens blaring'. Gordon's primary responsibility at the ATAO was overseeing one such checkpoint, by himself all year round, chasing natives, refugees, and smugglers that crossed the border, and either negotiating with or fighting them until he retrieved the Originium hallucinogens from their false teeth, or the live Originium slugs from their tails. His biggest achievement over the years was confiscating a crown with a hundred thirty-two foldartals pasted on it, owned by a Sami snowpriest. Three years passed before Gordon returned from the border checkpoints to the nomadic cities. At Tkaronto port, he was stopped by an excited young reporter who wanted to know if he was the outlaw hero Bluebeard. As Gordon got away from the reporter, he said: 'Sure, people were putting 'Originium' on everything they could think of, and you could say that the president guided Originium fever in the direction he wanted. But why did it have to be toothpaste? 'Took me three years to figure it out. Someone had the bright idea to corner the dental hygiene market with Originium floss, so he called on every favor he could to get this crazy prohibition through Congress. Buying and selling toothpaste was banned the next day. 'That's how the rules of ATAO came about. The rules that some people bleed to protect, and others bleed to defy. How does fighting them make you any kind of hero?'

I thought it was a thief when someone knocked on the door late at night, but it was a strangely dressed Savra who called himself Gordon Tannen. I remembered that my father had kept cursing that name the last time he came home, as though he were his actual son.
Gordon seemed very interested in everything in my house. The warped floorboards, the leaky roof, mom's red and swollen eyes, and my Gaulish accent that I could never fix. That, and my name: Gustave Baune. When Dad left, it was like he took Mom's soul with him. She missed him so much she changed my name to be the same as his, but I could never become him. He was the head of the ATAO, while I was a loser who was good for nothing but cleaning people's cars. When she begged him to give me a job at the ATAO, he slapped her.
Dad left because we weren't good enough for him. That, I accepted, but I didn't need pity from someone who WAS good enough for him... This Gordon, looking down at us from on high.
Thankfully, he didn't say much. Indeed, he didn't say anything at all for ten minutes, as we sat around a table silently, to the sound of Mom crying. He finally opened his mouth right when I was about to see him out.
'You won't be seeing your dad again. Treason. Life sentence.'
I already knew. The courts had sent a letter.
'You're allowed to change your name under Columbian law. Come find me if you want to change it back, or to something else.'
What he gave me was not a business card, but a bottle opener with a propeller on it, and the words 'Propeller Paradise' displayed prominently.
—Marlin Baune (formerly Gustave Baune), son of Gustave, former head of ATAO, in an interview with Maylander

'Gordon Tannen. You deny any private dealings with the traitor Gustave, but you have met with his son, Marlin Baune, multiple times following his incarceration, even inviting him to a tour of Propeller Paradise, where you were sighted drinking and partying with him. What is your explanation?'
'I was Gustave's former subordinate, and he was Gustave's son, so me visiting him means that I had dealings with Gustave—is that what you're implying?'
'Maylander cannot eliminate the possibility.'
'Wow, it's that easy working at Maylander? Okay, I'm reporting that pineapple pizza is evidence of a conspiracy between Siesta and Siracusa. When do I get my paycheck from you guys?'
'......'
'Listen, man. That kid Marlin cleaned cars for people in that border town for a decade. He's even smoother dealing with foreigners than I am. The only reason he's still cleaning cars is because old Gustave saw him as a disgrace. And what's worse, made the kid believe it himself. Let me tell you what I'm gonna do with him. I'm gonna open a bottle of champagne with him, and then I'm gonna get him a job at ATAO working at the city checkpoint, where he's gonna shine like he's never shined before. That's how ATAO's gonna be from now on. No freaking glory and no freaking shame. You got the chops, you got the job.'
—Interview with Gordon Tannen by Maylander investigators

Welcome to the Sky Conqueror solo exhibition. I am your guide, Space Fin 054. The tour is about to begin. Please turn off your mobile terminals. The first exhibit is a video disc set of the classic 70s drama, Sandwalker. Sandwalker, which depicts the exploits of a free-spirited Kuranta warrior, instilled a certain idea of freedom in an entire generation. Students often skipped class to play 'Sandwalker' on school grounds. Young Gordon did not join the other children's games after watching Sandwalker. But one afternoon, several trucks from a nearby construction site drove onto the school grounds, and turned it into a sea of sand in front of the stunned security guards. Nobody knows how Gordon fooled the foreman and security, but everyone remembers how he put on a cardboard helmet and raised his arm triumphantly before charging into the sea of sand. The schoolchildren had two hours of unprecedented fun before Gordon was dragged into the principal's office. Gordon said, 'If you're already skipping class, why settle for standing on the playground spouting lines from the show?' ...... Exhibit 13 is a game disc released in 1082 by Blue Box Co., Columbia. Gordon's approach to gaming is unusual. While this game is not considered particularly difficult, he played through each stage multiple times until he reached the inventory limit for all equipment and items, before challenging the final boss. The plan was to use this wealth of items to overcome the boss with ease. However, game discs at the time had a short lifespan, and it broke down when Gordon reached the final stage, so he never managed to beat the game. Gordon said, 'What's the point of reaching the boss if I don't crush him the first time?' ...... Finally, we have here a shrub from Sargon. Originally a tiny bud picked from a wooden stick, it has now entered its fifth generation under the nurturing of Gordon's 'Growth-Encouraging Loudspeaker' and 'Nutrition Lightbulb'. Today, every street tree in Propeller Paradise is a descendant of the original bud. Another 100 saplings have been sent to Rhine Lab, in the hopes that this tree that survived the harsh environment of the foehn hotlands can become the first plant to grow outside the Starpod. The item previously belonged to an explorer Gordon described as 'a hateful free spirit'. He apparently declined an invitation from the explorer to travel together, not because he was uninterested in going where no one had gone before, but because he saw no point in unburdened exploration. Gordon said, 'That budding stick would be nothing but a stylish walking stick in your hands. Give it to me, and I'll show you a moving forest the next time you see it.' ...... 'Excellent, Five-Four. Absolutely perfect. You finally understand my needs.' 'When will this exhibition be held, Sky Conqueror?' 'There's no rush. When I pry all of Columbia off the face of Terra and conquer the skies with everyone with super propellers.... that'll be the day. For now, your mission is to recite those descriptions to me every night before bedtime.'

A normally stoic Rhodes Island medic broke down in tears when he saw Rhodes Island medicine on the shelf of a Columbian drugstore.
In just six months, Rhodes Island's Oripathy medicine made rapid inroads into the Columbian market, which had been secluded itself for more than a decade. There is a long way to go until prices drop to a level affordable by the average Infected, but no one can deny that it is a huge first step.
Gordon Tannen, Chief Inspector of the ATAO, has never shunned any opportunity to flaunt his well-deserved pride as chief architect of this development. Following the incarceration of Gustave, former head of the ATAO, and the subsequent changing of the guard at the agency, Gordon Tannen has strengthened his own position while intentionally shredding the relationships that a certain corporation built into the ATAO for the purpose of enacting stringent Oripathy drug laws, enabling its monopoly.
However, rather than emphasize the help he rendered to Rhodes Island, Gordon boasts more often about 'building great things together with the Doctor'. Operators not in the know might believe him to be one of the Babel-era veteran, an elite operator operating undercover, after hearing him boast for two hours straight.
In fact, his first encounter with the Doctor was in Tkaronto four years ago, in an ATAO detention cell. Gordon had been working the border checkpoints for three years, and his only job in Tkaronto was to bring meals to the prisoners in the cells. At the same time, the Doctor had turned themself in in order to get the the ATAO to crack down on Mama John's, which had set a trap for Rhodes Island.
The dealings between the two of them began when the Doctor noticed a few extra meatballs in the dinner that Gordon brought.

'ATAO has every means at its disposal, and ATAO never fails. It's like a portable Arts unit with ready-to-cast Arts installed. All you need to do is aim and shoot, and anyone can buy one of those at an outdoor equipment shop for the price of a few hundred certs.
'The president can use it. Maylander can use it. Capitalists can use it. So why not us?
'That was the most important lesson I learned from the Doctor spending three days behind bars. And all it took was a few meatballs.'

lines.title: Appointed as Assistant
lines.text: We're filing project papers? You're kidding me. Why sit here sifting through the stuff we've already done…? There're denied proposals too? Then what the heck are we sitting here looking at dead trees for?

lines.title: Talk 1
lines.text: Let me guess. No, don't spoil it for me. Is this a smart head massager, or an autonomic pressure regulator cap, or a holographic environmental monitoring device…? It's just a normal hood? Well, dream bigger! Spot me some funding, and I'll do you a full suit worthy of the Head of Rhodes Island.

lines.title: Talk 2
lines.text: Yeah, I deal in contraband, but think—what am I 'violating'? They'd outlaw toothpaste if you paid 'em enough to make it Schedule 1. What kind of system is that? I'm trying to rescue the nice stuff from a contraband warehouse, you're trying to sell good drugs on the open market. You and me, we work the same.

lines.title: Talk 3
lines.text: Get a load of this, Doc! I rustled up an RGB frill-wig ahead of the summit on Originium goods regulations! Look, this thing changes color on its own, it… what? The summit started half an hour ago? Pfff. That's fine, I still gotta dip into the toybox. I'll deal with the summit later.

lines.title: Talk after Promotion 1
lines.text: It's not all eggheads at Propeller Paradise. Look at me, I learned all my physics from teaching toys. If I can make it in there, pretty much anyone with a brain can. I'm just out to match people with little fellas that work for them. Can you imagine anything better than that?

lines.title: Talk after Promotion 2
lines.text: Check that out. The stars. Glittering like a blanket over the sky. Make fun of me if you want, but when I was a kid, I'd hold this blanket full of holes over my head, stand under a light, look up to pretend I was stargazing. It was dumb. But life's about feeling out one dumb idea after another until you hit on something and feel like you've got your future. Right?

lines.title: Talk after Trust Increase 1
lines.text: What am I doing hanging upside-down from the ceiling? Ha! Well, you looked hot enough to boil in that suit, and my propeller here pulls double-duty as a fan, doesn't it? Y'know, excuse me in advance for this, but it's geniuses like you that stump me the most. How come you've got the brains to study a terminal disease, but you don't think to install yourself a better air conditioner?

lines.title: Talk after Trust Increase 2
lines.text: Back in Tkaronto, when I saw you squatting in the corner of your detention cell, chilling out studying the mushrooms, I knew the ATAO didn't get you, you were just playing the ATAO. And now here I am, business partner with a whiz like you. Goes to show I'm the real deal. And that I didn't put extra meat in your prison meals for nothing.

lines.title: Talk after Trust Increase 3
lines.text: Wait, what did you just call me? 'Friend'? Nooo no no no, I've used that word on a lot of people before, but not between us, you understand? I don't want to sully my most dependable associate with the kind of relationship that breaks down when you don't like the same food.

lines.title: Idle
lines.text: One of these days, I've gotta figure out a way to suck out all the wasted nutrients from the morons who can't use their brains, and then redirect them into you, so you can stop spending all this time sleeping.

lines.title: Onboard
lines.text: Want one, Doc? Here, I got a light. It's just an Originium firework, but you ain't seen nothing yet. Cut a deal today, and I'll get it to you tomorrow. Gordon Tannen, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Arts Units, and Originium, at your service.

lines.title: Watching Battle Record
lines.text: I got some bodycam footage from the gangs we busted back in my frontier days. Want it?

lines.title: Promotion 1
lines.text: This is a real deal promotion medal, and not my consolation prize for playing patsy, right? Hey, then this IS my first one ever. You wanna pop the champagne?

lines.title: Promotion 2
lines.text: I tell you what, this Rhodes Island joint's got potential to become the next Propeller Paradise! A few more of those promotions and I'll bring you along to make it happen… *burp*!

lines.title: Added to Squad
lines.text: You guys on the transport crew for my little fellas? Then I'll bring a few extra crates.

lines.title: Appointed as Squad Leader
lines.text: You guys remember one thing: When you kick the door down, kick like you mean it! I'll handle the rest.

lines.title: Depart
lines.text: Oh, high-explosive Originite grenade, my beloved, you'll waste away in the warehouse no longer. I'll blow you up so good the whole continent's gonna hear you scream.

lines.title: Begin Operation
lines.text: Get on your knees, now! What, never seen an ATAO agent lay down the law before?!

lines.title: Selecting Operator 1
lines.text: Don't sweat it, I catch your drift.

lines.title: Selecting Operator 2
lines.text: What, got a report for me?

lines.title: Deployment 1
lines.text: Keep it simple. Doesn't matter where you put me, I'm still headed for the skies.

lines.title: Deployment 2
lines.text: Stand a little further in, Doc. I can see your hood from here.

lines.title: In Battle 1
lines.text: Don't touch me! You gonna fix my hazmat suit too? It's called sense.

lines.title: In Battle 2
lines.text: No more hollering! What if I fill my data wrong? It's called courtesy.

lines.title: In Battle 3
lines.text: Get up! How do I test-fire if you're lying down? It's called responsibility.

lines.title: In Battle 4
lines.text: Quit playing dead! One more round, new weapon! It's called a control!

lines.title: 4-star Result
lines.text: Oh, high-explosive Originite grenade, my beloved, did you see that smoke, that fragmentation? You're a success, you're magnificent, you're a hundred KG yield!

lines.title: 3-star Result
lines.text: So I put the cuffs on you and now you say you got duped? What, did you forget you had a brain at the time?

lines.title: Sub 3-star Result
lines.text: Forget those runaways, tape, where's the duct tape? This is supercooled Originium condensate rustled from Sami! Every drop we lose, we lose forever!

lines.title: Operation Failure
lines.text: Book it, guys! I'm Gordon Tannen and I don't fear a damn thing! I'll give my life before I give my tail!

lines.title: Assigned to Facility
lines.text: Wow… What a beauty of a base. It's gotta be either an earth-digger or a sky-flier, right?

lines.title: Tap
lines.text: Feels good, right? Pure stress relief in your hand. It's designer. I'm always touching it myself.

lines.title: Trust Tap
lines.text: Yeah? Wanna come fly with me?

lines.title: Title
lines.text: Arknights.

lines.title: New Year's blessing
lines.text: Here's a toast to… eugh. Look at me, dredging up my old bootlicking ATAO habits. I'm throwing off our whole collaboration as equals. Okay, here's what we'll do. You serve as a tester for my new gear later, and then we're even again. Sound good?

lines.title: Greeting
lines.text: What's on your mind, Doc? Penny for your thoughts.

lines.title: Birthday
lines.text: C'mon, Doc, got a few hundred li'l fellas still waiting to meet you. Just you wait, they're gonna give you history's greatest firework show… What do you mean 'too much'? Too much my ass. Frankly, you should have your birthday every day, 'cause hunting for an excuse to do this is a pain in my tail.

lines.title: Anniversary Celebration
lines.text: Propeller Paradise, Rhodes Island, we're all relegated to roaming the barrens alone. But someday, there'll be a hundred Propeller Paradises and a hundred Rhodes Islands sailing all over the place. We'll be the great land then, and it'll be Max D.C.'s turn to be the languid lonely little dinghy.
